summary: Skardu International Airport (KDU) is a vital gateway to the Gilgit-Baltistan region of northern Pakistan, serving as the primary air access point for trekkers, climbers, and tourists heading to the Karakoram and Himalayan ranges, including K2. Situated in a valley at an elevation of approximately 2,230 meters (7,310 feet), it is one of the highest commercial airports in the world. The airport has grown in importance as adventure tourism in the region has expanded, offering stunning aerial views of snow-capped peaks during approach and departure.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Skardu International Airport?
A: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the primary carrier operating scheduled flights to Skardu from Islamabad, with occasional services from other Pakistani cities.

Q: What is the best time of year to fly to Skardu?
A: The most reliable flying weather typically occurs from May to October, with summer and early autumn offering the best conditions. Winter flights are frequently delayed or cancelled due to poor visibility and weather.

Q: How high is Skardu Airport above sea level?
A: Skardu Airport sits at an elevation of approximately 2,230 meters (7,310 feet), making it one of the highest commercial airports in the world.

Q: Are there international flights to Skardu?
A: Currently, Skardu Airport primarily handles domestic flights. Travelers typically connect through Islamabad International Airport for international arrivals.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers from Skardu town center, and taxis and jeeps are readily available outside the terminal for the short ride into town. Road travel between Islamabad and Skardu is possible but takes approximately 18-24 hours via the Karakoram Highway, so flying is strongly recommended to save time. Flights are weather-dependent, so always build buffer days into your itinerary when planning onward travel or treks.
local_tip: Pack motion sickness remedies for the flight, as the approach into Skardu's narrow valley often involves dramatic turns and turbulence, especially when mountain wind conditions are active.
